purpose: Teach: 吹か/絵柄/被る/亡き/女将/桶/安物/小豆

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが秋風を吹かれた庭で読書された
lines.en: You know, dear, when I was young, my father used to read out in the garden with the autumn wind blowing over him.
lines.style: Slow, low, contemplative opening. Long unhurried phrases, gazing into the memory, softening on the image of the garden.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、絵柄、つまり古い絵柄の着物を私に下さったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Mm, and when you were young, dear, you gave me that kimono with the old-fashioned pattern, didn't you?
lines.style: Gentle affirming hum to open. Warm, teasing affection rising into the tag question at the end.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが「不運を被る事は誰にもある」と仰った
lines.en: When I was young, my father once told me, 'Misfortune can befall anyone.'
lines.style: Measured and grave, the quote delivered slowly with quiet reverence, like handling something fragile.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、亡き友人を偲んで俳句を詠まれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you, dear — when you were young, you composed haiku in memory of your late friend, didn't you?
lines.style: Soft and careful, voice thinning with feeling on the late friend, ending on a gentle upward tag.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが旅館の女将さんと懇意にされた
lines.en: In his younger days, my father was on friendly terms with the mistress of an inn — the okami.
lines.style: A faint smile in the voice now, reminiscing pace, small approving weight on the okami.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、井戸の桶で水を汲まれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: You used to draw water with the well bucket when you were young, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Light, fond amusement. Slightly quicker lilt, gently prodding him to remember, warm on the closing 'dear.'

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは「安物買いの銭失い」と諭された
lines.en: My father used to admonish me: 'Buy cheap and you throw your money away.'
lines.style: Dry, rueful chuckle under the proverb. Deliberate delivery of the old saying, self-mocking warmth at the memory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、小豆ご飯で祝い事をされたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And in those days we marked every celebration with adzuki rice, didn't we, dear?
lines.style: Warm, settling close. Slow contented pace, the memory sweet in her mouth, ending soft and satisfied.
